boundedApproaches.name: Keep positions 1–3 as source-referenced tutorial lessons
boundedApproaches.why: Their scope is deliberately small and has very low topology entropy: one edge, then a path of two or three edges. Treating these as reference lessons avoids manufacturing apparent novelty with tiny coordinate/angle perturbations. If new content is required here, target a structural addition (one extra ring plus a new authored pin dependency) and withhold it until physical validation.

boundedApproaches.name: Small branch/merge lesson from native pin motifs
boundedApproaches.why: Use 5–9 ring pieces with a distinct branch/hub dependency or multiple connected components, based on source pin assignments and graph motifs rather than shuffled whole ring poses. Preserve exact source atomic templates and source-feature pin roles; create new links only by exact feature sockets and rerun raw seam/contact and native release validation.

boundedApproaches.name: Introduce one Pull mechanic via a complete guide motif
boundedApproaches.why: Retain a complete fixed-guide host→Pull pair (never a loose Pull-only visual) and its actual guide shape indices. Add one small 3–5 ring pin motif through a compatible native socket. This raises a small lesson to roughly 8–13 parts with a genuinely new interaction while limiting scope.

boundedApproaches.name: Use same-grid ring banks with changed dependency maps as semantic candidates
boundedApproaches.why: The native corpus contains multiple 24-ring puzzles over exactly repeated center grids with materially different directed pin graphs and attachment assignments. Learn or assemble dependency motifs over stable spatial scaffolds; keep a separate semantic-structure comparison alongside the unchanged whole-layout geometric check.

inherentLimits: A two-ring, one-edge lesson has almost no structural alternatives while preserving its teaching objective; cosmetic pose changes are not strong novelty evidence.
The current geometry near-copy criterion can certify geometric non-copy only; it cannot decide that a changed pin graph makes a new puzzle or that the puzzle is playable.
Merging whole native motifs is a proposal method, not proof: all moved or newly joined pins need exact socket relations, raw geometry checks, native solver replay, and independent difficulty review.
Do not promise a fully novel 2–4-piece generated tutorial under strict source-fidelity and source-near-copy rejection without relaxing the target scope or adding a real mechanic.

layoutNoveltyV3PairAudit.interpretation: The novelty heuristic ignores authored links and pin feature identities. Zero near-copy outcomes here reflect its geometric pose/template thresholds and do not establish puzzle-level originality.

concreteSameScaffoldExample.sourceEvidence: Both appear as separate original source IDs/progression entries in the full 500 pack; their authored link maps differ despite the same center grid. This is evidence of distinct source-level structure, not a claim of verified solvability or player-perceived novelty.

semanticNearCopyRecommendation.additiveMetric: Keep layout_novelty_v3 geometric output unchanged and add a separate informational puzzle-structure distance after geometric alignment: compare directed owner edges, native sourceFeature/targetFeature and attachment IDs, relation/activity kinds, guide host/locked Pull features, bomb ownership, and attached pin/head geometry in matched owner-local frames.
semanticNearCopyRecommendation.interpretation: Report visual scaffold near-copy and puzzle-graph divergence as separate axes. A high geometry match plus large graph edit should be flagged for expert review as a reused scaffold with changed interaction structure, not silently treated as fully novel or as identical gameplay.
semanticNearCopyRecommendation.limitation: Source structure differences are observable, but without native replay they remain unverified rule-level dependencies.
